description: A proxyfile: one gateway, the services behind it and the routes to them, from which proxyfile writes the proxy's configuration.

admin.description: The port of the admin listener, on 127.0.0.1; no admin listener when not written.

auth.description: The checks every request goes through before it reaches a service: a service of yours asked about each request, a signed token the proxy verifies, or both.

accept.description: The headers of the check's answer that reach the service; a name ending in * is a prefix.

ask.description: The service and the path the gateway asks.

enabled.description: true runs the check on every request it applies to, false on none.

jwt.description: The proxy verifies a signed token (a JWT) on each request itself: its signature against your keys, its issuer, its audience and its expiry.

audiences.description: The audiences accepted: a token's aud must hold one of them, or any accepts every audience.

ca.description: The CA bundle, PEM, the keys URL's certificate must chain to; /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt when not written.

additionalProperties.description: The claim it holds, with dots for a nested claim.

claims.description: Claims copied into request headers for the service, by header name.

header.description: The header that carries the token; authorization, with the Bearer scheme, when not written.

issuer.description: The iss claim a token must carry.

keys.description: Where the signing keys come from, as a JWKS: a file on the proxy's host, or an https URL the proxy fetches and keeps for 10 minutes.

optional.description: true lets a request with no token through unverified; a request with a token that fails is still refused. false when not written.

only_with_header.description: The check runs only on requests that carry this header.

send.description: The request headers the check is sent; a name ending in * is a prefix.

send_request.description: true also tells the check which request it is asked about: its path and query in x-forwarded-uri, its method in x-forwarded-method, its scheme in x-forwarded-proto and its host in x-forwarded-host; false when not written.

timeout.description: How long the gateway waits for the answer.

when_unavailable.description: What happens to a request when the check cannot be asked: allow lets it through, deny refuses it.

client_address.description: Which address counts as the client's: forwarded, the last address a proxy in front appended to X-Forwarded-For, or connection, the peer of the TCP connection.

cors.description: The CORS settings every environment shares.

max_age.description: The value of Access-Control-Max-Age: how long a browser may keep a preflight answer.

dns.description: The name lookups of every DNS name the gateway reaches: a service's address, the tracing endpoint and the keys URL's host.

resolver.description: The name server the proxy asks; the host's own resolver configuration when not written.

envoy.description: The settings only the Envoy generator reads: the namespace of the gateway's metadata, its heap budget, the old place of tracing and the Connect bridge.

connect_bridge.description: true turns each Connect call on an RPC route into gRPC for the service, and the answer back into Connect; false routes gRPC calls alone. true when not written.

heap.description: The heap budget: the gateway shrinks its heap at 90% of it and refuses new requests at 98%.

namespace.description: The namespace of the gateway's own metadata, which the routes and the request log use; proxyfile when not written.

tracing.description: The old place of tracing, read in every 2.x release with the xray provider only; 3.0 removes it.

path_in_url.description: true keeps the request's path in the span's URL, its first 256 characters; false, the default, keeps the scheme and the host only.

provider.description: The tracing system the spans go to: a mapping with one key that names it.

xray.description: AWS X-Ray: where the segments go, their name and which requests are traced.

agent.description: Where the segments go over UDP: an X-Ray daemon, or an agent that takes X-Ray segments; 127.0.0.1:2000 when not written.

sample.description: Which requests are traced when the request does not say: the rules, then the default. Without it, Envoy traces the first request each second and 5% of the others.

first.description: How many requests each second are traced before rate applies; 1 when not written.

rate.description: The share of the other requests that is traced; 5% when not written.

rules.description: Rules tried in the order written, before the default; the first that matches a request decides.

items.description: One rule: what it matches, and its own first and rate.

first.description: How many matching requests each second are traced before rate applies.

host.description: Matches the Host header, with its port when the request has one; * when not written.

method.description: Matches the request's method; * when not written.

path.description: Matches the request's path, with its query; * when not written.

rate.description: The share of the other matching requests that is traced.

segment.description: The name of the gateway's segments, which names its node in X-Ray's service map.

additionalProperties.description: One tag: the environment variable or the request header it reads, and an optional default.

default.description: The value when the variable is unset or the header is absent; without it the span gets no tag then.

env.description: An environment variable of the gateway's process, read once when Envoy starts.

tags.description: Tags on each span, by name.

haproxy.description: The settings only HAProxy will read; this version has no HAProxy generator, so it takes no key.

limits.description: Limits on connections and request headers.

connections.description: The most connections at once, from clients and to each service.

request_headers.description: The largest header block and the most header fields a request may carry.

count.description: The most header fields in a request.

size.description: The largest header block of a request.

listen.description: The port of the public listener, on 0.0.0.0.

log.description: Which requests the request log writes.

sample.description: The share of the other requests that is logged.

status_from.description: The lowest status that is always logged.

nginx.description: The settings only nginx will read; this version has no nginx generator, so it takes no key.

origins.description: The browser origins each environment admits, by environment name; or, as in 1.0, the name of an origins file, relative to this file.

additionalProperties.description: One environment: its hosts and the browser origins it admits.

hosts.description: The host names the environment serves, without a port.

origins.description: The browser origins admitted exactly, each scheme://host[:port].

patterns.description: The browser origins admitted by pattern, where * matches any run of characters.

remove_from_clients.description: Headers removed from every client request before routing and before any filter; a name ending in * is a prefix.

routes.description: The routes, tried in the order written; the rpc entry marks where the RPC routes go.

oneOf.description: The place in the order where the RPC routes go.

rpc.description: The RPC routes: one exact-path route for each RPC method.

rate_limit.description: How many requests the route admits in a period; a request over the limit is answered 429 and never reaches the service.

burst.description: Extra requests admitted above requests after a quiet spell; 0 when not written.

by.description: client counts each client address on its own, all every client together; client when not written.

retries.description: How many times an RPC call that never reached its service is tried again.

oneOf.description: The service the methods go to.
The service the methods go to, and the name of their routes.

name.description: The name of the routes; the service's name followed by -rpc when not written.

service.description: The service the methods go to.

to.description: The service the RPC methods of each package go to.

oneOf.description: A route: a name, what it matches and the service it goes to.

auth.description: off sends the route's requests to the service without auth's checks: no service is asked and no token is verified.

method.description: Matches only requests with this HTTP method.

pattern.description: Matches paths by this regular expression, in RE2 syntax.

prefix.description: Matches paths that start with this text.

rate_limit.description: How many requests the route admits in a period; a request over the limit is answered 429 and never reaches the service.

burst.description: Extra requests admitted above requests after a quiet spell; 0 when not written.

by.description: client counts each client address on its own, all every client together; client when not written.

retries.description: How many times a request that never reached the service is tried again.

rewrite.description: Replaces the matched prefix or path before the request goes to the service.

to.description: The service the route goes to.

rpc.description: The RPC methods the gateway routes; the routes' rpc entry maps them to services.

methods.description: One entry for each RPC method the gateway routes, as a build writes them from the gRPC descriptors.

action.description: The action the check is told for this method.

reports.description: The reports the check is told for this method.

service.description: The full name of the method's service.

proto.description: The RPC methods, read from the .proto files under roots: each method that carries the method option named by option.

option.description: The full name of the method option that marks a method the gateway routes.

roots.description: The directories of .proto files, each an import root: relative to the proxyfile's directory, or absolute.

additionalProperties.description: One service: a port per protocol, an optional Host header, its backends, how requests are spread over them and how they are checked.

address.description: The service's IP address, or a DNS name the proxy looks up again while it runs; 127.0.0.1 when not written.

addresses.description: The service's backends, by IP address, each on the service's ports.

balance.description: How requests are spread over the backends; round_robin when not written.

hash.description: What balance hash hashes, so that one client or one header value always reaches the same backend.

client.description: true hashes the client's address, the one client_address names.

header.description: The request header whose value is hashed; a request without it goes to a backend chosen at random.

health.description: Active checks of each backend: one that fails unhealthy checks in a row leaves the pool until it passes healthy checks in a row.

grpc.description: true checks the service's grpc port with the gRPC health protocol, grpc.health.v1.Health/Check.

healthy.description: Checks in a row a backend must pass to join the pool; 2 when not written.

interval.description: How often each backend is checked; 5s when not written.

path.description: The path an HTTP GET must answer with a 2xx, on the service's http port.

timeout.description: How long one check may take; 2s when not written.

unhealthy.description: Checks in a row a backend must fail to leave the pool; 3 when not written.

host_header.description: The Host header a request carries when a route sends it to this service.

services.description: The services behind the gateway, by name.

timeouts.description: How long a request, an idle request and an idle connection to a service may last.

idle.description: The longest a request may go without sending or receiving data.

request.description: The longest a whole request may take.

upstream_idle.description: The longest a connection to a service is kept open with no request on it.

tls.description: The public listener serves HTTPS with this certificate and key; without it, plain HTTP.

certificate.description: The certificate chain, PEM, a file on the proxy's host.

clients.description: Require a client certificate on every connection (mutual TLS).

ca.description: The CA bundle, PEM, that a client's certificate must chain to.

key.description: The private key, PEM, a file on the proxy's host.

tracing.description: A trace span for each sampled request, sent to AWS X-Ray or to an OpenTelemetry collector.

path_in_url.description: true keeps the request's path in the span's URL, its first 256 characters; false, the default, keeps the scheme and the host only.

provider.description: The tracing system the spans go to: a mapping with one key that names it.

xray.description: AWS X-Ray: where the segments go, their name and which requests are traced.

agent.description: Where the segments go over UDP: an X-Ray daemon, or an agent that takes X-Ray segments; 127.0.0.1:2000 when not written.

sample.description: Which requests are traced when the request does not say: the rules, then the default. Without it, Envoy traces the first request each second and 5% of the others.

first.description: How many requests each second are traced before rate applies; 1 when not written.

rate.description: The share of the other requests that is traced; 5% when not written.

rules.description: Rules tried in the order written, before the default; the first that matches a request decides.

items.description: One rule: what it matches, and its own first and rate.

first.description: How many matching requests each second are traced before rate applies.

host.description: Matches the Host header, with its port when the request has one; * when not written.

method.description: Matches the request's method; * when not written.

path.description: Matches the request's path, with its query; * when not written.

rate.description: The share of the other matching requests that is traced.

segment.description: The name of the gateway's segments, which names its node in X-Ray's service map.

otel.description: OpenTelemetry: spans sent as OTLP over gRPC to a collector.

endpoint.description: Where the spans go, as plain OTLP over gRPC: a collector beside the gateway or in its network.

sample.description: Which requests are traced; one whose traceparent says it is not sampled never is.

rate.description: The share of the requests that is traced; 5% when not written.

service.description: The service.name the spans carry, which names the gateway in the tracing backend.

additionalProperties.description: One tag: the environment variable or the request header it reads, and an optional default.

default.description: The value when the variable is unset or the header is absent; without it the span gets no tag then.

env.description: An environment variable of the gateway's process, read once when Envoy starts.

tags.description: Tags on each span, by name.
